text: You think Everest is the highest point on Earth?
Correct. Please clap.
But stand here, and you're two kilometers closer to space and to the sun.
Hi, you're standing on me.
A sleepy volcano in Ecuador, about 2,600 meters shorter than Everest.
So how is this shorter mountain closer to the stars?
Rewind to 1802, when many thought Chimborazo was Earth's highest mountain.
Explorer Alexander von Humboldt climbed to about 5,875 meters,
higher than any European before.
Then, altitude sickness sent him back down.
I have that effect on people.
In the 1850s, surveyors in India measured the Himalayas,
and Chimborazo got demoted.
Sorry, champ.
So how did the loser end up closest to space?
Because Earth isn't a perfect ball.
It spins, so it bulges at the equator.
The equator sits about 21 kilometers farther from the center than the poles.
Earth has a belly, and Chimborazo sits just one degree from the equator.
Ecuador literally means equator.
Everest, about 28 degrees north.
Measured from Earth's center, Chimborazo's peak is 6384 kilometers out.
Everest, 6382.
Everest wins from the sea.
Chimborazo wins from the core.
Here's the twist.
Everest isn't even in the top 20.
Even Kilimanjaro beats me?
Even Kilimanjaro.
So who's on top of the world?
Depends where you measure from.
This is Bughal.
